findings.title: RSS/feed content is stored and rendered as unsanitized raw HTML
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations, and Post#cook returns raw verbatim for such posts. The PollFeed path passes feed-supplied i.content (only CGI.unescapeHTML) with no sanitization, unlike import_remote which at least restricts Readability tags/attributes. findings.title: Referer is interpolated unescaped into JavaScript and misused as postMessage targetOrigin
findings.body: request.referer is attacker-influenced (the embedding page / a crafted link can control it within the allowed host check on host only, and its path/query are unchecked) and is inserted verbatim inside a single-quoted JS string: a referer containing `'` or `</script>` breaks out and executes arbitrary script in the Discourse origin inside the iframe. Separately, postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]), not a full URL with path, so passing the whole referer makes browsers drop the discourse-resize message and iframe resizing silently never works. Emit only the referer's origin, escaped with a JS/JSON encoder (e.g. to_json).

findings.title: postMessage origin check is a substring test, not an origin equality test
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any e.origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. a truncated/scheme-only-looking origin or a host that is a prefix of the configured URL string), rather than requiring exact equality with the Discourse origin. Any such sender page can then drive the discourse-resize handler and resize the embed iframe. Parse discourseUrl to its origin and compare `e.origin === thatOrigin` exactly.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content (and on Ruby without String#scrub)
findings.body: SimpleRSS items frequently lack a `content` element (using description/summary instead or nothing), so `i.content` is nil and `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting poll_feed mid-loop so remaining items are never imported and the hourly job fails every run for such a feed. String#scrub is also Ruby 2.1+, while this codebase supports Ruby 1.9-era installs, where it raises NoMethodError for every item. Guard with `(i.content || i.description || '').to_s` and a compatible encoding cleanup.

findings.title: Feed-supplied URL is interpolated unescaped into an HTML anchor
findings.body: The imported_from suffix builds `#{url}` directly from the feed/retrieved URL. import() only checks the URL starts with http(s)://; a URL containing a single quote, `<`, or `&` (obtainable from a feed item's link/id, which PollFeed accepts) breaks out of the href attribute and injects arbitrary markup into the raw_html post, compounding the stored-XSS risk, and at minimum produces malformed links. HTML-escape the URL and attribute-escape/validate it before interpolation.

findings.title: Embed controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever the controller no longer uses
findings.body: The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example sets `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, but EmbedController#best implements retrieval via `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)` and never references TopicRetriever. Mocha will fail this expectation at teardown and the actual enqueue arguments are untested, so the spec suite goes red / gives false confidence. Rewrite it to expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic and the correct user_id/embed_url.
